goal: RA-8375 revision 3: as revision 2 (worktree-mode session start works from any Pi-Dev-Ops checkout on any machine; the two hook lines call .claude/hooks/worktree_hook.py, which reads the event from standard input), and in addition the script hands its version-control calls no GIT_* variable from its caller, so only the folder the script decided on chooses which repository is read and changed. Reason: CodeRabbit on c40ebe7a showed that an inherited GIT_DIR made the removal step take a worktree holding a commit on no branch, and made the creation step build a worktree of another repository. The guard tests for that live in a second test file because the first is at the repository's 300-line cap.

criteria.text: The worktree hook tests pass, including the guard tests that set a GIT_* variable in the hook's environment, together with the existing class guards that run every registered hook (no hook exits 2 when its script is missing; missing targets stay quiet).

Since its merge base with main the branch changes exactly these files and no others: the hook script, the settings file, .gitignore, the two test files, and the three Done contract folders for this work (the first contract and its two revisions).

criteria.text: The settings file no longer reads WORKTREE_DIR or WORKTREE_BRANCH, the two variables Claude Code never sets.
The suite keeps tests that run the old hook lines against Claude Code's real input and require them to fail, so the reason for the fix stays reproducible.
The script and both test files pass the repository's lint.
The repository's own .gitignore ignores .claude/worktrees/, so a worktree made by the hook does not show as an untracked folder on a machine without this Mac's local exclude file.

With GIT_DIR in the hook's environment naming this project's own main checkout, the removal step still keeps a worktree that holds a commit on no branch. This is the case CodeRabbit reported on c40ebe7a; the test was seen failing on that commit's script.
